changed_request: Only ontology in user payload; new provider rules, same source and8 questions, service parameters unchanged.

decisions.rationale: No alarm is mentioned anywhere; the utterance content is entirely a taxi booking for a flight-arrival pickup, so no alarm kind, purpose or category is expressed.

No application or software service is named or used as the means of performing the activity; no registered lexical expressions (tweet, Google-as-search) appear, and generic 'book a taxi' does not identify an application.
No music creator or musical performer role is expressed; the only person reference (Shelley Hennessey) is a pickup passenger with no singing/song/music relation.
'Book' occurs only as a travel-booking verb ('book a taxi'), which per the author rules supplies no book-author relation; no book or audiobook is referred to, so no authorship role exists.
No particular identifying reference to a book or audiobook is expressed; 'book' is the booking verb for a taxi, not a work reference, and no work role or title appears.

'AA' is attached to a represented transport service ('the arrival of aa flight five thousand four hundred and thirty one'), which per the provider-role rule expresses its operator as part of the service attribution; an identifying name suffices without acronym expansion or corporate lookup.
'Book a taxi' requests a transportation service as an offered-service category, explicitly matching the business_type definition's example of booking a taxi as a described service.
No control adjustment magnitude or desired target level is expressed anywhere in the utterance; the quantities present are a flight number and a clock time, which are not adjustment levels.
